topic: Life Cycles of Major Plant Groups
title: Which Phase Do We See? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
A moss on the wall, a fern in a pot and a mango tree in the yard all have two phases, one with a single chromosome set and one with two. Diya asks a sharp question: which phase are we actually looking at?

You will see the three patterns of plant life cycle run as living cycle diagrams: haplontic (Volvox, Spirogyra, some Chlamydomonas), diplontic (gymnosperms, angiosperms, Fucus) and haplo-diplontic (bryophytes, pteridophytes, Ectocarpus, Polysiphonia, kelps), with the dominant phase and the place of meiosis marked in each. Then the three patterns side by side, a pause and think check, a worked example for each plant, the exam trap, an original NEET pattern matching question, a recap card and three questions to answer. This is Episode 29 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and NEET students.
